title: Reducing an exact finite free complex modulo a nonzerodivisor keeps exactness one step less
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a local ring, $e\ge2$ an integer and $0\to R^{\oplus n_e}\xrightarrow{\varphi_e}R^{\oplus n_{e-1}}\xrightarrow{\varphi_{e-1}}\cdots\xrightarrow{\varphi_1}R^{\oplus n_0}$ a complex of finite free $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-free-module] ($\varphi_i\circ\varphi_{i+1}=0$ for $1\le i\le e-1$) which is exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] at $R^{\oplus n_e},R^{\oplus n_{e-1}},\dots,R^{\oplus n_1}$. Let $x\in\mathfrak m$ be a nonzerodivisor of $R$ ($xy=0$ implies $y=0$), $\bar R=R/xR$, and $\bar\varphi_i:\bar R^{\oplus n_i}\to\bar R^{\oplus n_{i-1}}$ the $\bar R$-linear map whose matrix [def-weil-matrix] is the matrix of $\varphi_i$ with its entries reduced modulo $x$ (equivalently $\varphi_i\otimes_R\bar R$). Then the complex $0\to\bar R^{\oplus n_e}\xrightarrow{\bar\varphi_e}\bar R^{\oplus n_{e-1}}\to\cdots\xrightarrow{\bar\varphi_2}\bar R^{\oplus n_1}$ is exact at $\bar R^{\oplus n_e},\bar R^{\oplus n_{e-1}},\dots,\bar R^{\oplus n_2}$.

proof.text: For consecutive matrices A and B with Function.Exact A.mulVec B.mulVec, lift a reduced A-cycle v to w using surjectivity of the coordinate quotient map. Since q(Aw)=0, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem and Ideal.mem_span_singleton give Aw=x t coordinatewise. Exactness implies B(Aw)=0, so x Bt=0. Cancel the nonzerodivisor x coordinatewise to obtain Bt=0, and use exactness to write t=Az. Then w-x z is an A-cycle reducing to v. This is the fully proved private helper lift_reduced_cycle; matrix reduction commutes with mulVec by RingHom.map_mulVec.

Apply the cycle-lifting helper at degree e using exactness at e-1. If two reduced vectors have the same image under the reduced top matrix, their difference is a cycle. Lift that difference to a cycle for the original top matrix; hinjective forces the lift to be zero. Thus the reduced difference is zero and the reduced top matrix is injective.

For 2 <= i < e, use the helper and exactness at i-1 to lift any reduced cycle to an original cycle. Exactness at i supplies a preimage under phi_(i+1); its reduction maps to the original reduced cycle. For the converse inclusion, lift a reduced boundary preimage coordinatewise, apply hcomplex, and commute reduction with both matrix maps. This proves the required Function.Exact at every interior degree. The original theorem signature is unchanged.
